papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 13 Practice Paper (Linear Equations & Intercepts)

questions.question_text: Where does the line 2x + 3y = 12 intersect the X-axis?
How many ordered pair solution sets (x, y) satisfy the linear equation 3x - 2y = 7?
Find x-intercept and y-intercept for line 4x - 5y = 20.
Write 2x = 3y - 5 in standard form ax + by + c = 0 and identify coefficients a, b, c.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Standard form: 2x - 3y + 5 = 0. Coefficients: a = 2, b = -3, c = 5.

questions.question_text: Graph 2x + y = 6 and x - y = 0 on a Cartesian plane. Find the intersection point and verify algebraically.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Line 1 intercepts: (0, 6), (3, 0). Line 2 points: (0, 0), (2, 2). Intersection graph point: (2, 2). Algebraic verification: Substitute y = x into 2x + x = 6 => 3x = 6 => x = 2, y = 2.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Taxi Fare Model. Fixed charge x plus rate y per km. 10 km trip costs Rs 105; 15 km trip costs Rs 155. (a) Formulate linear system. (b) Find x and y. (c) Calculate cost for 25 km trip.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) System: x + 10y = 105 and x + 15y = 155. (b) Subtracting: 5y = 50 => y = Rs 10/km. Substitute: x + 100 = 105 => x = Rs 5 fixed charge. (c) Fare for 25 km = 5 + 25(10) = Rs 255.

papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 13 Practice Paper (Slope & Line Classification)

questions.question_text: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if the product of their slopes m1 * m2 equals:
What is the slope of horizontal line y = 5?
Find slope and y-intercept of line 3x + 4y - 12 = 0 by converting to y = mx + d form.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 4y = -3x + 12 => y = (-3/4)x + 3. Slope m = -3/4, Y-intercept d = 3.

questions.question_text: Determine k for UNIQUE solution: kx + 2y = 5 and 3x + y = 1.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: a1/a2 != b1/b2 => k/3 != 2/1 => k != 6. Unique solution for all real k except 6.

questions.question_text: Classify linear systems (unique, no solution, infinite solutions) using coefficient ratios for: (1) 2x + 3y = 9 & 4x + 6y = 18, (2) x + 2y = 4 & 2x + 4y = 12.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. a1/a2 = 2/4 = 1/2, b1/b2 = 3/6 = 1/2, c1/c2 = 9/18 = 1/2. Coincident lines -> INFINITELY MANY solutions. 2. a1/a2 = 1/2, b1/b2 = 2/4 = 1/2, c1/c2 = 4/12 = 1/3. a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2. Parallel lines -> NO solution (Inconsistent).

questions.question_text: Case Study: Temperature Conversion Line. F = (9/5)C + 32. (a) Find F when C = 30 deg. (b) Find C when F = 95 deg. (c) Find temperature where F and C values are numerically equal.

papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 13 Practice Paper (Point-Line Distance & Systems)

questions.question_text: Perpendicular distance from origin (0, 0) to line 3x + 4y - 10 = 0 is:
Slope of vertical line x = 4 is:
Calculate perpendicular distance from (0,0) to 3x + 4y - 10 = 0 using distance formula.
Find k for infinite solutions: 2x + 3y = 7 and 6x + ky = 21.
Solve algebraic elimination system: 2x + 3y = 9 and 3x + 4y = 13.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Multiply Eq 1 by 3: 6x + 9y = 27. Multiply Eq 2 by 2: 6x + 8y = 26. Subtract: y = 1. Substitute y = 1 into Eq 1: 2x + 3(1) = 9 => 2x = 6 => x = 3. Solution (3, 1).

questions.question_text: Case Study: Supply and Demand Intersection. Demand: p = -2q + 20. Supply: p = 3q + 5 (where p is price, q is quantity). (a) Find equilibrium quantity q and price p. (b) Explain economic meaning of graph intersection point.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Set equal: -2q + 20 = 3q + 5 => 5q = 15 => q = 3 units. Price p = 3(3) + 5 = $14. (b) Graph intersection point (3, 14) is market equilibrium where buyers' demand quantity equals sellers' supply quantity.

papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 13 Practice Paper (Applied Linear Formulations)

questions.question_text: If (2, -1) lies on line 2x + ky = 8, then k equals:
Area of triangle formed by line x + y = 6 with coordinate axes is:
Substitute (2, -1) into 2x + ky = 8 to solve for k.
Calculate area of right triangle formed by line x + y = 6 with axes.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: X-intercept (6, 0), Y-intercept (0, 6). Base = 6, Height = 6. Area = 1/2 * base * height = 1/2 * 6 * 6 = 18 sq units.

questions.question_text: A two-digit number is 4 times the sum of its digits. If 18 is added to the number, the digits reverse. Formulate linear system and find the number.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Let tens digit be x, units digit y. Number = 10x + y. Eq 1: 10x + y = 4(x + y) => 6x - 3y = 0 => 2x - y = 0. Reversed number = 10y + x. Eq 2: 10x + y + 18 = 10y + x => 9x - 9y = -18 => x - y = -2. Subtracting: x = 2. Then y = 4. Number is 24.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Boat Stream Speed System. A boat travels 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours. It travels 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream in 13 hours. (a) Let u = 1/(x-y) and v = 1/(x+y). Formulate linear system. (b) Find boat speed x in still water and stream speed y.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) System: 30u + 44v = 10 and 40u + 55v = 13. (b) Solving yields u = 1/5 and v = 1/11. Thus x - y = 5 (upstream speed) and x + y = 11 (downstream speed). Adding: 2x = 16 => x = 8 km/h (boat speed). y = 3 km/h (stream speed).

papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 13 Practice Paper (Exhaustive Unit Test)

questions.question_text: Equation of line parallel to X-axis passing through (3, -4) is:
Distance between parallel lines 2x + 3y = 6 and 2x + 3y = 19 is:
Find parallel line distance formula step-by-step for 2x + 3y = 6 and 2x + 3y = 19.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Distance d = |c2 - c1| / sqrt(a^2 + b^2) = |19 - 6| / sqrt(2^2 + 3^2) = 13 / sqrt(13) = sqrt(13) units.

questions.question_text: If line pass through (1, 2) and (3, 8), calculate slope m and equation in y = mx + d form.
Find coordinates of vertices of triangle formed by lines 2x - y = 4, x + y = 2, and Y-axis. Calculate triangle area.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Line 1 on Y-axis (x=0): (0, -4). Line 2 on Y-axis (x=0): (0, 2). Intersection of Line 1 and 2: Add equations => 3x = 6 => x = 2, y = 0 -> (2, 0). Base along Y-axis = 2 - (-4) = 6 units. Height = x-coordinate of intersection = 2 units. Area = 1/2 * 6 * 2 = 6 sq units.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Production Cost Line. Fixed overhead $500 plus variable cost $15 per unit. (a) Write linear cost equation C(x). (b) If selling price is $25 per unit, write revenue equation R(x). (c) Calculate break-even unit count.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Cost C(x) = 15x + 500. (b) Revenue R(x) = 25x. (c) Break-even where R(x) = C(x) => 25x = 15x + 500 => 10x = 500 => x = 50 units.
